hero.title: I build small, sharp tools that live in the browser.
hero.sub: Client-side apps with a game-dev streak — canvas pipelines, keyboard-first UX, and pixel-level polish. Everything below runs live on your machine: no uploads, no servers.

work.title: Live tools, not screenshots
work.sub: Every project below is the real thing — embedded and running in your browser. Open one and use it.

video-to-gif.desc: A tiny cutting room: trim, crop and caption a clip, then encode it into a looping GIF — or MP4/WebM — entirely client-side, with Discord-ready size presets.

image-compressor.desc: Drop in images and squeeze the excess weight out. Live re-encoding through the canvas API with quality, format and size controls — nothing leaves your device.

typing-speed-test.desc: A telegraph-flavored typing test. The clock starts on your first keystroke, accuracy counts as much as speed, and personal bests persist per duration.

contact-sheet.desc: Lay photos out into a print-ready PDF contact sheet — grid, paper size and margins, rendered in the browser with jsPDF. A whole darkroom in a single HTML file.

about.title: Hands in code, eyes on the browser
about.p1: I'm Giorgi — a developer who likes building small, finished things: tools you can open, use and understand in a minute. My favorite playground is the browser, where canvas, WebGL and a good keyboard shortcut can replace a whole desktop app.
about.p2: Lately that means client-side media tools and game-flavored interfaces — encoding GIFs in a web worker, squeezing images through canvas, measuring words per minute down to the keystroke. This portfolio is part of the collection too: React, Three.js, Express, and two languages.
